title: Voice line
description: Character dialogue, barks and narration with Qwen3-TTS (Apache 2.0). Design a voice from a description, or name a saved character `voice` so every line keeps the same voice.
prompt_guide: `prompt` is exactly the words to speak. `voice_description` says who speaks: age, gender, accent, timbre, pace - e.g. 'An old man with a deep gravelly voice and a slow, weary Scottish accent'. `emotion` says how this line is said: 'angry, shouting', 'whispering, afraid'. Give a `voice` id to keep a character consistent across lines: the first call creates the voice from the description, later calls reuse it.

param_help.voice_description: who is speaking and how they sound (used to create a voice)
param_help.language: Auto, English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian or Italian
param_help.model_choice: size of the cloning model for saved voices: 1.7B or 0.6B (quicker)
param_help.unload_after: free the voice model's VRAM after each line (slower, for small cards)
param_help.candidates: how many takes to generate; the one that best matches the prompt (CLAP) and passes the checks is kept
param_help.trim: cut silence at the start and end
param_help.trim_db: what counts as silence, in dB below the clip's peak
param_help.loop: make the file loop seamlessly (the end is crossfaded into the start)
param_help.max_seconds: cut the result to at most this many seconds
param_help.channels: mono (sounds placed in the 3D world - engines pan them), stereo (UI, ambience, music) or keep
param_help.loudness: integrated loudness target in LUFS; null leaves the level alone. Starting points: SFX -16, UI -16, voice -18, music -18, ambience -24
param_help.peak_db: the peak never goes above this (dBFS); the gain is lowered instead of clipping
param_help.sample_rate: resample to this rate (e.g. 48000); null keeps the model's own rate
param_help.keep_candidates: keep every take in .soundforge/<name>/ next to the result

fast.description: The smaller cloning model for saved voices.

max.description: Three takes with less variation; the first clean one is kept.
